title: Squid Game
hook: How does Squid Game end? The failed rebellion, the newborn player, and Gi-hun's final sacrifice in the Season 3 finale, explained.

sections.heading: After the rebellion fails
sections.body: Season 3 opens in the wreckage of the failed uprising from the previous season. Most of the rebels are executed, and only a handful, including Seong Gi-hun, survive into the new round of games. The remaining players vote to keep playing despite the slaughter, choosing the prize money over solidarity. Gi-hun, Player 456, carries the weight of the rebellion's collapse and the deaths it cost. The season pushes him through a series of escalating lethal challenges, including a deadly hide-and-seek, a jump-rope crossing, and the final round, while his faith that people can be better than the game steadily erodes.

sections.heading: The baby who becomes a player
sections.body: A central thread is the newborn child of the player Jun-hee, born inside the game and assigned the number 222 after Jun-hee's death. The infant becomes an official competitor, its survival tied to the rules like any other player. The baby comes to symbolise the next generation, the future that the adults around it keep deciding to gamble on or protect. Several characters' choices in the back half of the season pivot on whether the child should be shielded or sacrificed, and the question of the baby's fate becomes the moral spine that the entire finale is built around.

sections.heading: The Sky Squid Game
sections.body: The final round, the Sky Squid Game, forces the last players to push one another off elevated towers. It comes down to Gi-hun, Myung-gi and the baby. Myung-gi reveals he is the child's biological father, but he intends to sacrifice the infant to claim the prize and win. Gi-hun refuses to let the baby die. Rather than compete to survive or kill the father, he makes a different choice entirely, deciding that the child's future matters more than his own life and that he will not become the thing the game wants him to be on the tower.

sections.heading: Gi-hun's fall and the next recruiter
sections.body: Gi-hun throws himself off the platform, sacrificing his life so the baby wins and survives. Player 222, the newborn, takes the prize money. Hwang In-ho, the Front Man, rescues the child as the island is evacuated and leaves with the VIPs. Detective Hwang Jun-ho survives among the other escapees. Six months later in Los Angeles, In-ho visits Gi-hun's daughter to tell her of his death and deliver his bloodied tracksuit and remaining winnings. The final shot reveals an American recruiter playing ddakji, signalling the games are spreading to the United States.

final_image: On a Los Angeles street, an American recruiter crouches over a game of ddakji, the deadly games quietly seeding themselves in a new country after Gi-hun's death.

lingering_questions.q: Who actually wins Squid Game in the final season?
lingering_questions.a: The winner is Jun-hee's newborn, Player 222. Gi-hun sacrifices himself by jumping off the tower so the baby survives and receives the prize money, framing the next generation as the victor.

lingering_questions.q: What does the Los Angeles ending mean?
lingering_questions.a: Six months after Gi-hun's death, the Front Man delivers his winnings to his daughter, and a final scene shows an American recruiter playing ddakji. It signals the games are expanding into the United States.
